process_note: First reported on #34 as probably my own CPU contention: the file runs last in FILE_ORDER and I had run a 55-second board-free pytest in that window. The clean idle re-run reproduced it, so the self-blame was refuted. A plausible self-blame is still a hypothesis and still needs its control run - and it is more tempting than the other kind because accepting it costs nothing.
arms_note: All three arms are immutable commits. The third was 'current main' until mac-bench pointed out it was the one arm a later fix could make meaningless, so it was re-run pinned at f3cad64.

fix.licenses: the regression is gone at the rate this reproducer can see
fix.does_not_license: 'fixed'. 0 of 20 bounds the rate under 15%, not at zero, and #44's own 11-of-32 sits well inside that. Doubled from ten deliberately: at n=10 the rule of three reaches only 30%, a weaker claim than a bare '0 of 10' reads as.
fix.why_the_shape_is_right: Opening the gate when the drain ends rather than when start() does satisfies both invariants without depending on what start() happens to do afterwards. The earlier sketch rested on 'start() does no native reads after cmd()', true today and breakable silently by a future settle-read.

open: the Linux arm, linux-x1's, and the informative branch
